request_state.literature: Literature (primary source arXiv:2412.11933, survey of solved cases): fully solved with all exponents>=3 are (3,3,n) for n<=10^9, (n,n,3) for n>=3, (n,n,n) for n>=3. Effective-finiteness only (not solved): (2p,2q,r) with p,q>=V_r [arXiv:2509.21083]. NOT solved: (4,4,5), (4,4,7), (4,6,3), any (2m,2n,r odd) with m!=n, (3,5,7), (5,5,7).
request_state.claim: Exact reduction of the sparsest mod-72 class (x,y even, z odd): a counterexample there is exactly a coprime opposite-parity pair (u,v) with Re((u+vi)^z) and Im((u+vi)^z) both perfect powers (exponents >= 2), and C = u^2+v^2. Derivation: C is odd (kernel-verified not_both_exponents_even_of_even_C), so a+bi, a-bi are coprime in the UFD Z[i]; units are z-th powers for z odd. Box search u,v<=400, z in {3,5,7}: 194,970 pairs, zero hits.
